# CLI reference

`protoboard` (alias `pb`) is the command-line interface of the Protoboard Stack, in `@protoboardai/cli`.
Every command takes `--format json` for machine output and `--cwd <dir>` for the project
directory (default: the current one, or the nearest folder above it with a `protoboard.config.ts`).
`protoboard --version` prints the CLI's version, and with `--json` where the build came from (commit,
uncommitted changes, branch, and whether it is a release); `protoboard <command> --help` prints this help
without running the command.

The [quickstart](../quickstart.md) walks through these commands in order;
[configuration](configuration.md) covers the files and environment variables they read.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `init <dir>` | Scaffold a portable Protoboard project; --template drone\|wearable\|iot starts from a template derived from a reference project, and vendors its catalog parts from the parts service (--no-parts skips that). The project's cloud.url is the hosted Protoboard library (--url or PROTOBOARD_CLOUD_URL for another; --local for http://localhost:8787). --list shows the templates; --name names the project (default: the folder name); --registry <url> writes an .npmrc that takes @protoboardai/* and @deltarobotics/* from that registry (default: the registry npm ran this CLI from, when it is not npmjs) The project uses the Protoboard installed for your user (--stack global, the default): its packages are links to the copy in ~/.protoboard/stack, so check, build, dev and the viewer work with no npm install in the project. The copy is the one the VS Code extension carries, or, for a CLI that npm installed, one this command installs there once per version. --stack project (and --registry) installs the packages into the project with npm instead: its npm install then exports its extensions' skills to .claude/skills/ and lists them in AGENTS.md (a postinstall script; --no-skills leaves it out). The last lines say how to open the project in a new VS Code window |
| `init --refresh-guidance [dir]` | In an existing project: bring AGENTS.md's Protoboard guidance (the shared sections, between its markers) to this version's and keep the project's own sections, write a CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md when there is none, and export the skills list; lines elsewhere that contradict the guidance are reported, not rewritten |
| `upgrade [dir]` | Move a project made by an earlier Protoboard (0.1.x) to this version: package.json's @protoboardai/* ranges become ^0.2.0 and its UHD and TypeScript pins this stack's, its packages are linked again to a stack copy that fits, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md get this version's guidance (init --refresh-guidance) and vendored parts move to the current layout (parts migrate). Offline; --dry-run lists the changes and writes nothing. Commit the project first, then run `protoboard check` |
| `inspect [instance]` | System summary, or one instance's definition, origin, links, artifacts, diagnostics |
| `artifacts [instance]` | Artifacts of the definitions in use (or of one instance), with the instances using them and the file each resolves to |
| `check` | Resolve the project and run every available validator (exit 1 on errors) |
| `build` | Write .protoboard/build/resolved.json (derived data only) |
| `layout [level]` | The diagram's layout measured, level by level, as the viewer draws it: line crossings, overlapping cards, the longest row or column of cards (a strip), the aspect ratio and lines under cards, with what to fix. A level is an instance path ("" is the top; default: every level). --apply lays the level(s) out afresh, --tidy keeps the saved arrangement and fixes it; either writes .protoboard/display.json where the result reads better (--force: anyway). --pin <card> keeps a card where it is (repeatable; remembered in the file). --check: exit 1 when a level still has something to fix. check reports the levels of modules that need it as PB_DIAGRAM_LAYOUT (info) |
| `views check` | The viewer's tabs for the root and every level with modules inside it (--module <instance path or module id> for one), each opened once in a headless browser: fails (exit 1) on a tab that throws, shows an empty state or draws nothing. --out-dir <folder> keeps a PNG of every tab; --no-render only lists the tabs |
| `dev` | Serve the UHD viewer on the project: rebuilds on every source change, saves diagram layout edits to .protoboard/display.json (--port, --host, --open, --no-watch) |
| `bom` | The bill of materials, by top-level module, in US dollars: what one unit needs, the offer used for each line, what must be bought (whole packs, minimum orders), the cost per unit and the cost of the order. --units <n> builds n (default: the project's setting, else 1); --release <version> lists that release's ordering list instead of the design; --format json carries everything, --format csv is the export. Offline: prices are the offers the project holds |
| `bom units <n>` | Set the units to build (parts/bom.json) |
| `bom offers <line>` | The offers held for a line (its part id or ordering code), best first |
| `bom choose <line> <offer\|supplier\|auto>` | Use that offer for the line (parts/bom.json); auto goes back to the best offer |
| `parts list` | The project's parts: library parts (pinned revision; diverged when their vendored files were edited), researched (parts/local) and designed (src/). Offline; --check asks the libraries which have an update |
| `parts search [words]` | Search every part library, results merged with the library each comes from (--taxonomy, --domain, --protocol, --tag, --limit, --library; --facets adds counts; --cursor <c> gives the next page, from the previous page's nextCursor). --sort relevance\|name\|manufacturer\|updated orders them, in a library that sorts (relevance, the library's own ranking, is its default; --format json carries each part's relevance value) |
| `parts taxonomy` | The libraries' category taxonomy merged, with part counts over --domain, --protocol, --tag and the words given |
| `parts add <id[@rev]...>` | Vendor library revisions (default: the recommended one) with their closure and files into parts/catalog, pinned in parts/origins.json. The part comes from the first library that has it, unless --library names one or origins pins one. Its .uhd.ts source comes too (linted, and checked to evaluate to the pinned definition); --compiled vendors the definition JSON only |
| `parts migrate` | Move vendored parts from the folder layout of 0.1.6 and earlier (which repeats the part id in every path, too long for Windows in a nested project) to the short one; offline, the pins stay. check reports PB_CATALOG_LAYOUT_EARLIER (info) while there are some |
| `parts update [id...]` | Show the recommended revision of vendored parts and what it changes; writes nothing |
| `parts update <id> --to <rev\|recommended>` | Deliberately re-pin a vendored part (the replaced pin is kept as previous); --library moves it to another library; --compiled as for add |
| `parts offers [id...]` | Vendor the service's supplier offers for catalog parts into parts/offers.json (what a release quotes offline; replaces those parts' entries) |
| `parts prices <id>` | A library part's prices by source: each supplier's price breaks, stock, pack and minimum order, the link and when it was observed (--mpn for one ordering code of a series part). Needs a signed-in account; writes nothing |
| `parts publish <path>` | Publish a project-researched part (parts/local) as its next catalog revision (needs a publisher: signed in as one, or PROTOBOARD_CLOUD_TOKEN; --dry-run shows the revision without publishing) |
| `login` | Sign in to Protoboard Cloud (the parts service at --url, else the project's cloud.url, else, outside a project, the hosted Protoboard library): a browser sign-in, or --device for agents and machines without a browser (a code to approve on the sign-in site). The sign-in goes to Linux's keyring, Windows' DPAPI, else a file only you can read; never to the project. Everything in the library needs it: search, adding parts, prices and downloads |
| `logout` | Forget the sign-in for the service at --url |
| `whoami` | Who is signed in to the service at --url (--check asks the service) |
| `libraries` | The project's part libraries in order (--check asks each for its discovery document) |
| `libraries add <id> <url> [--auth-env PROTOBOARD_<NAME>_TOKEN] [--position n]` | Add a uhd-library/v1 library (last unless --position); with only <url>, its discovery document suggests the id. --auth-env names the environment variable holding its read token; tokens are never written to the project |
| `libraries remove <id>` | Remove a library (parts vendored from it stay vendored) |
| `libraries move <id> <position\|first\|last\|up\|down>` | Reorder: the first library that has a part id provides it. Personal libraries (not in the project) come from PROTOBOARD_USER_LIBRARIES, a JSON array of { id, url, authEnv? }; they are searched after the project's |
| `doctor` | Extensions, compatibility, tool availability, runtimes, skills, the sign-in and where the stack's packages come from. Its Build line says whether this is a release or a development build, and the commit it was built from when known |
| `stack` | Where this CLI and the project's packages come from: installed by npm, or links to a stack copy in ~/.protoboard/stack (the copy the VS Code extension carries) |
| `stack link` | Link the project's Protoboard packages to the Protoboard installed for your user: a stack copy that fits the project (its range, its packages), this CLI's own version first, and it says when it takes another (what Initialize does in VS Code, with no npm and no registry); --force re-points links that lead to another copy; --carried links the copy this CLI runs from whatever package.json asks. npm-installed packages are never replaced. Every command warns when the project links to another version |
| `stack unpack [<extension folder \| .vsix>]` | Unpack the stack a Protoboard VS Code extension carries into ~/.protoboard/stack, as the extension does when it starts (its archives checked against their digests), then link the project to it when it fits. With no path: the installed extension of this CLI's version, else the newest installed (`protoboard stack` lists them). A copy of the same version from another build is replaced only with --replace |
| `setup` | Set up the rest of this machine, with no sign-in: install the Protoboard extension (deltarobotics.vscode-protoboard) into VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium (those whose command is found; it asks about each, --yes does not), from the Marketplace or Open VSX through each editor's own command, or from --vsix <file> offline; then offer to put the protoboard command on your PATH and to connect your agents (agents setup). Never runs by itself |
| `stack install` | Install the stack version package.json pins into ~/.protoboard/stack/<version> from a registry (needs npm; --registry <url>), then link the project to it; --from-vsix <extension folder \| .vsix> is `stack unpack` |
| `tools` | Tool runtimes the extensions declare, and whether they are installed here |
| `tools install <cad\|circuit\|all>` | Create the project's runtime in .protoboard/tools/ (a Python venv or Node packages, exact pins from the extensions) and record it; probes, checks and operations then use it without environment setup (--python <interpreter> makes the venv; --clean starts over) |
| `skills` | List installed skills |
| `skills read <name> [file]` | Print a skill's SKILL.md (or one of its files, such as references/<file>), by name: how AGENTS.md tells an agent to read one, on any machine |
| `skills export --host <claude-code\|agents-md\|all>` | Put the skills where an agent host discovers them: .claude/skills/ (claude-code), a list in AGENTS.md (agents-md), or both (all). A project made by init runs it at the end of npm install (--on-install: both, one line, never fails) |
| `extensions add <name...>` | Add an extension to the project (ext-tscircuit, tscircuit and @protoboardai/ext-tscircuit are one): package.json and protoboard.config.ts list it, it is linked from the Protoboard installed for your user (no npm), and its skills are exported. A project that installs its own packages (--stack project) fetches it with its next npm install |
| `run <operation>` | Run an extension operation (--input key=value; --authorize for external/physical) |
| `run <capability>:<op> --module <instance path or module id>` | Run a capability operation (generate\|export\|extract\|check, or one the provider adds, such as circuit:lock) through the provider named by the module's <capability>.config.ts; --force for one that takes it |
| `capabilities` | Capabilities, their providers, and which modules use which provider |
| `operations` | List operation records |
| `release [--version <v>]` | Write the Manufacturing Package to release/<version>/ (@protoboardai/ext-release). Refused while check reports errors, an output is stale or the project has uncommitted changes (--allow-dirty records them; --check only reports) |
| `evals` | Run the eval cases that installed extensions ship in evals/: each trial works on a scratch copy of the case's fixture, then is graded; scorecard and summary go to .protoboard/evals/<run>/ (--extension, --case, --trials, --jobs, --host, --judge, --model, --no-skills, --keep, --work-dir, --out-dir, --list, --ci) |
| `agents` | The agents found on this machine (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cline) and whether each has Protoboard's MCP server configured. Reads only |
| `agents setup` | Add the MCP server to the agents' configuration, so an agent knows Protoboard from the start. Asks about each agent; without a terminal, --agent <id> (repeatable) or --all, with --yes. Changes only Protoboard's entry, keeps a copy of the file before its first write, and says what it wrote where. With the first yes it also writes Protoboard's launcher into its own folder. --scope project writes the project's own file (.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, …) |
| `agents remove` | Take the MCP server out again (the same options) |
| `agents config` | The command, JSON and steps for any other MCP client. Prints only |
| `agents refresh` | Write or update Protoboard's launcher (in its own folder; no agent's file), for a client set up by hand from agents config |
| `mcp` | The Protoboard MCP server on stdio: what an agent starts (it takes no arguments) |

## Options

Options prefixed with a command name (`dev:`, `evals:`) apply to that command only.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--format text\|json` | Output format (default text); --json is the same as --format json. `protoboard --version --json` adds the build: commit, dirty, branch, source, release |
| `--cwd <dir>` | Project directory (default: current) |
| `--url <service>` | parts: the Protoboard library's URL (default PROTOBOARD_CLOUD_URL, then cloud.url in protoboard.config.ts, then http://localhost:8787). Only parts commands, init --template (its catalog parts) and login, logout and whoami use it; those three, run outside a project, default to the hosted Protoboard library instead of localhost. |
| `--library <id>` | parts: the library to use (search: only that one) |
| `--compiled` | parts add, parts update --to: vendor the definition JSON only, not its .uhd.ts source |
| `--device` | login: sign in with a code approved on another device (the default when this terminal has no browser: no TTY, CI, SSH or no display) |
| `--severity <level>` | check: lowest severity to print (error\|warning\|info, default warning) |
| `--module <ref>` | run <capability>:<op>: instance path (board) or module id (watch-mainboard) |
| `--port <n>` | dev: first port to try (default 5180; taken ports are skipped unless given) |
| `--host <addr>` | dev: interface to bind (default 127.0.0.1) |
| `--open` | dev: open the viewer in the default browser |
| `--no-watch` | dev: serve the current build without watching |
| `--host-origin <origin>` | dev: origin of a window framing the viewer that may drive it and hear its events (repeatable; scheme://* and * allowed; default: the page's own origin and VS Code webviews) |
| `--allow-host <name>` | dev: a Host name the server answers besides the loopback names, for a proxy that forwards the external one (repeatable; * answers any: only behind a proxy that authenticates, as a browser-hosted VS Code's) |
| `--python <path>` | tools install: interpreter that creates a Python venv (default: the first Python found that works; the ones refused are listed with the reason) |
| `--clean` | tools install: delete the runtime's folder first |
| `--version <v>` | release: the release version (default: the root module's version) |
| `--allow-dirty` | release: release from uncommitted changes (recorded in the manifest) |
| `--check` | release: run the preconditions only; write nothing. libraries: ask each library for its discovery document. layout: exit 1 when a level has a warning |
| `--apply` | layout: lay the level(s) out afresh and write the display file where it reads better |
| `--tidy` | layout: start from the saved arrangement, fix what reads badly, and write it |
| `--pin <card>` | layout: a card (node id on that level) that keeps its place (repeatable) |
| `--extension <id>` | evals: one extension (@protoboardai/ext-parts, ext-parts or parts) |
| `--case <id>` | evals: one case, a pattern with * (author-*), or several, comma-separated |
| `--trials <n>` | evals: trials per case (default 1) |
| `--jobs <n>` | evals: fixtures and trials to run at once, across cases, into one scorecard (default 1) |
| `--no-skills` | init: no postinstall that exports the skills (npm run skills:export does it by hand). evals: the ablation arm: no skills exported, their documents left out of the module mirror, no Skill tool |
| `--on-install` | skills export: what a project's postinstall runs: both hosts, one line of output, nothing when no skill is installed, and never a failure |
| `--host <agent>` | evals: scripted (default; replays each case's known-good steps) or claude-code (Claude Code headless: claude -p, no MCP servers, no user settings, the case's tools only, inside the scratch copy) |
| `--judge <judge>` | evals: claude-code scores rubric graders (default: off, rubric graders skipped) |
| `--model <model>` | evals: the model for the claude-code host and judge |
| `--keep` | evals: keep the fixture and trial directories |
| `--work-dir <dir>` | evals: scratch folder (default: the system temp folder) |
| `--out-dir <dir>` | evals: where scorecards go (default: .protoboard/evals in the project) |
| `--list` | evals: list the cases without running them |
| `--agent <id>` | agents setup, remove: one agent (repeatable); the ids are in agents --format json |
| `--all` | agents setup, remove: every detected agent |
| `--yes` | agents setup, remove: do not ask (needs --agent or --all). setup: install the extension into every editor found, and add the command to PATH, without asking |
| `--stack global\|project` | init: where the project's packages come from (default global: links to the Protoboard installed for your user; project: installed into the project with npm) |
| `--vsix <file>` | setup: install this extension package instead, offline (default: the extension by its id, from the Marketplace or Open VSX) |
| `--editor <id>` | setup: only this editor (code, cursor, windsurf or codium; repeatable) |
| `--no-agents` | setup: leave the agents' configuration alone |
| `--scope user\|project` | agents: your own configuration (default) or the project's shared file. A project's entry is "npx --no-install protoboard mcp" when the project depends on the CLI (--portable forces that, --no-portable writes this machine's launcher) |
| `--ci` | evals: the CI hook: scripted host only, exit 1 on any failed trial or broken case |

```text
                            the stack's packages come from. Its Build line says whether this is a release or a
                            development build, and the commit it was built from when known
    stack                   Where this CLI and the project's packages come from: installed by npm, or links to a
                            stack copy in ~/.protoboard/stack (the copy the VS Code extension carries)
    stack link              Link the project's Protoboard packages to the Protoboard installed for your user: a
                            stack copy that fits the project (its range, its packages), this CLI's own version
                            first, and it says when it takes another (what Initialize does in VS Code, with no
                            npm and no registry); --force re-points links that lead to another copy; --carried
                            links the copy this CLI runs from whatever package.json asks. npm-installed packages
                            are never replaced. Every command warns when the project links to another version
    stack unpack [<extension folder | .vsix>]
                            Unpack the stack a Protoboard VS Code extension carries into ~/.protoboard/stack, as
                            the extension does when it starts (its archives checked against their digests), then
                            link the project to it when it fits. With no path: the installed extension of this
                            CLI's version, else the newest installed (`protoboard stack` lists them). A copy of
                            the same version from another build is replaced only with --replace
    setup                   Set up the rest of this machine, with no sign-in: install the Protoboard extension
                            (deltarobotics.vscode-protoboard) into VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium (those
                            whose command is found; it asks about each, --yes does not), from the Marketplace or
                            Open VSX through each editor's own command, or from --vsix <file> offline; then offer
                            to put the protoboard command on your PATH and to connect your agents (agents setup).
                            Never runs by itself
    stack install           Install the stack version package.json pins into ~/.protoboard/stack/<version> from a
                            registry (needs npm; --registry <url>), then link the project to it;
                            --from-vsix <extension folder | .vsix> is `stack unpack`
    tools                   Tool runtimes the extensions declare, and whether they are installed here
    tools install <cad|circuit|all>
                            Create the project's runtime in .protoboard/tools/ (a Python venv or Node
                            packages, exact pins from the extensions) and record it; probes, checks and
                            operations then use it without environment setup (--python <interpreter>
                            makes the venv; --clean starts over)
    skills                  List installed skills
    skills read <name> [file]
                            Print a skill's SKILL.md (or one of its files, such as references/<file>), by name:
                            how AGENTS.md tells an agent to read one, on any machine
    skills export --host <claude-code|agents-md|all>
                            Put the skills where an agent host discovers them: .claude/skills/ (claude-code),
                            a list in AGENTS.md (agents-md), or both (all). A project made by init runs it
                            at the end of npm install (--on-install: both, one line, never fails)
    extensions add <name...>
                            Add an extension to the project (ext-tscircuit, tscircuit and
                            @protoboardai/ext-tscircuit are one): package.json and protoboard.config.ts list it,
                            it is linked from the Protoboard installed for your user (no npm), and its skills
                            are exported. A project that installs its own packages (--stack project) fetches it
                            with its next npm install
    run <operation>         Run an extension operation (--input key=value; --authorize for external/physical)
    run <capability>:<op> --module <instance path or module id>
                            Run a capability operation (generate|export|extract|check, or one the
                            provider adds, such as circuit:lock) through the provider named by the
                            module's <capability>.config.ts; --force for one that takes it
    capabilities            Capabilities, their providers, and which modules use which provider
    operations              List operation records
    release [--version <v>]
                            Write the Manufacturing Package to release/<version>/ (@protoboardai/ext-release).
                            Refused while check reports errors, an output is stale or the project has
                            uncommitted changes (--allow-dirty records them; --check only reports)
    evals                   Run the eval cases that installed extensions ship in evals/: each trial works on
                            a scratch copy of the case's fixture, then is graded; scorecard and summary go to
                            .protoboard/evals/<run>/ (--extension, --case, --trials, --jobs, --host, --judge,
                            --model, --no-skills, --keep, --work-dir, --out-dir, --list, --ci)
    agents                  The agents found on this machine (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code,
                            Windsurf, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cline) and whether each has Protoboard's MCP server
                            configured. Reads only
    agents setup            Add the MCP server to the agents' configuration, so an agent knows Protoboard from
                            the start. Asks about each agent; without a terminal, --agent <id> (repeatable) or
                            --all, with --yes. Changes only Protoboard's entry, keeps a copy of the file before
                            its first write, and says what it wrote where. With the first yes it also writes
                            Protoboard's launcher into its own folder. --scope project writes the project's
                            own file (.mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .vscode/mcp.json, …)
    agents remove           Take the MCP server out again (the same options)
    agents config           The command, JSON and steps for any other MCP client. Prints only
    agents refresh          Write or update Protoboard's launcher (in its own folder; no agent's file), for a
                            client set up by hand from agents config
    mcp                     The Protoboard MCP server on stdio: what an agent starts (it takes no arguments)

  Options
    --format text|json      Output format (default text); --json is the same as --format json.
                            `protoboard --version --json` adds the build: commit, dirty, branch, source, release
    --cwd <dir>             Project directory (default: current)
    --url <service>         parts: the Protoboard library's URL (default PROTOBOARD_CLOUD_URL, then cloud.url in
                            protoboard.config.ts, then http://localhost:8787). Only parts commands, init
                            --template (its catalog parts) and login, logout and whoami use it; those three,
                            run outside a project, default to the hosted Protoboard library instead of
                            localhost.
    --library <id>          parts: the library to use (search: only that one)
    --compiled              parts add, parts update --to: vendor the definition JSON only, not its .uhd.ts
                            source
    --device                login: sign in with a code approved on another device (the default when this
                            terminal has no browser: no TTY, CI, SSH or no display)
    --severity <level>      check: lowest severity to print (error|warning|info, default warning)
    --module <ref>          run <capability>:<op>: instance path (board) or module id (watch-mainboard)
    --port <n>              dev: first port to try (default 5180; taken ports are skipped unless given)
    --host <addr>           dev: interface to bind (default 127.0.0.1)
    --open                  dev: open the viewer in the default browser
    --no-watch              dev: serve the current build without watching
    --host-origin <origin>  dev: origin of a window framing the viewer that may drive it and hear its
                            events (repeatable; scheme://* and * allowed; default: the page's own origin
                            and VS Code webviews)
    --allow-host <name>     dev: a Host name the server answers besides the loopback names, for a proxy that
                            forwards the external one (repeatable; * answers any: only behind a proxy that
                            authenticates, as a browser-hosted VS Code's)
    --python <path>         tools install: interpreter that creates a Python venv (default: the first
                            Python found that works; the ones refused are listed with the reason)
    --clean                 tools install: delete the runtime's folder first
    --version <v>           release: the release version (default: the root module's version)
    --allow-dirty           release: release from uncommitted changes (recorded in the manifest)
    --check                 release: run the preconditions only; write nothing. libraries: ask each
                            library for its discovery document. layout: exit 1 when a level has a warning
    --apply                 layout: lay the level(s) out afresh and write the display file where it reads better
    --tidy                  layout: start from the saved arrangement, fix what reads badly, and write it
    --pin <card>            layout: a card (node id on that level) that keeps its place (repeatable)
    --extension <id>        evals: one extension (@protoboardai/ext-parts, ext-parts or parts)
    --case <id>             evals: one case, a pattern with * (author-*), or several, comma-separated
    --trials <n>            evals: trials per case (default 1)
    --jobs <n>              evals: fixtures and trials to run at once, across cases, into one scorecard (default 1)
    --no-skills             init: no postinstall that exports the skills (npm run skills:export does it by
                            hand). evals: the ablation arm: no skills exported, their documents left out of
                            the module mirror, no Skill tool
    --on-install            skills export: what a project's postinstall runs: both hosts, one line of output,
                            nothing when no skill is installed, and never a failure
    --host <agent>          evals: scripted (default; replays each case's known-good steps) or claude-code
                            (Claude Code headless: claude -p, no MCP servers, no user settings, the case's
                            tools only, inside the scratch copy)
    --judge <judge>         evals: claude-code scores rubric graders (default: off, rubric graders skipped)
    --model <model>         evals: the model for the claude-code host and judge
    --keep                  evals: keep the fixture and trial directories
    --work-dir <dir>        evals: scratch folder (default: the system temp folder)
    --out-dir <dir>         evals: where scorecards go (default: .protoboard/evals in the project)
    --list                  evals: list the cases without running them
    --agent <id>            agents setup, remove: one agent (repeatable); the ids are in agents --format json
    --all                   agents setup, remove: every detected agent
    --yes                   agents setup, remove: do not ask (needs --agent or --all). setup: install the
                            extension into every editor found, and add the command to PATH, without asking
    --stack global|project  init: where the project's packages come from (default global: links to the Protoboard
                            installed for your user; project: installed into the project with npm)
    --vsix <file>           setup: install this extension package instead, offline (default: the extension by its
                            id, from the Marketplace or Open VSX)
    --editor <id>           setup: only this editor (code, cursor, windsurf or codium; repeatable)
    --no-agents             setup: leave the agents' configuration alone
    --scope user|project    agents: your own configuration (default) or the project's shared file. A project's
                            entry is "npx --no-install protoboard mcp" when the project depends on the CLI
                            (--portable forces that, --no-portable writes this machine's launcher)
    --ci                    evals: the CI hook: scripted host only, exit 1 on any failed trial or broken case
```
